note: Company (organisation) page rubric. Use instead of rubric.json when the profile is a LinkedIn company page, not a person. Score honestly.

items.full_marks: Names the buyer and what changes for them, carries one piece of proof, uses most of the 120 characters. Not a slogan on its own.
The first two lines (before 'see more') name the reader and their problem. Does not open with the company name or 'founded in'.
Services as outcomes, how the firm works, one or more verifiable proof points, and a clear next step with a contact. Under 2,000 characters.
Branded cover with one line of positioning; nothing important under the logo overlap on the left. Not a stock image or default.
Square mark that reads at 60 px, on a background that matches the brand.
Industry, size, type, primary location, one website consistent with all other materials, and a custom button set.
Up to 20 specialties using the terms buyers actually search for.
A pinned post that is current (under 60 days) and is the best proof or lead asset.
Recurring long-form content (LinkedIn newsletter or articles) published from the page.
Leaders and employees list the page as current employer and have headlines that name the buyer.
At least two posts a week for the last month, and comments on page posts answered within a day.
